title: Purgatory and Prayers for the Dead
lead: The Catholic teaching that those who die in God's grace but are not yet fully cleansed are purified after death. Orthodox, Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican and Baptist churches differ, from praying for the dead without a doctrine of purgatory to rejecting it as unbiblical.

sections.b: 1 Corinthians 3:10-15 (saved "as through fire") is the passage most often argued over. 2 Maccabees 12:38-46, where Judas Maccabeus has an offering made for the fallen, is the other main text; Catholic and Orthodox churches count 2 Maccabees as Scripture, and Protestants do not. Others cited are Matthew 12:32 and 1 Peter 3:19. Whether any of them teaches purgatory is itself disputed.

sections.h: A teaching that grew over centuries
sections.b: The early church prayed for the dead and spoke of a testing fire (Origen, Augustine, Gregory the Great). Purgatory as a defined place and process was taught by the Councils of Lyon II (1274) and Florence (1439) and Trent (1563). The Reformers rejected it; Orthodox churches hold prayers for the dead without the Latin teaching of purifying fire and satisfaction.
